chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He in whose heart is a mustard seed of prejudice (tribalism/partisanship), Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment along with the Bedouins of the Pre-Islamic period.'

key_terms.أَعْرَابِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: The Bedouins of the Pre-Islamic period (era of ignorance)
key_terms.حَبَّةٌ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ: A mustard seed (indicating a small but significant amount)

ai.seo_question: What does a mustard seed of prejudice mean in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi is pivotal for defining 'asabiyyah' not merely as tribal loyalty but as a spiritual defect that negates Islamic equality, linking it directly to the moral decay of the Pre-Islamic era. The comparison to a 'mustard seed' underscores that even a minuscule amount of this bias is sufficient to categorize an individual with the 'A'rab al-Jahiliyyah', emphasizing the severity of the sin in the Hereafter. This concept is often cited by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid to critique social stratification and partisan politics within the Muslim community.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one in whose heart was a mustard seed of prejudice in his heart, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Resurrect him on the Day of Judgment along with the Bedouins of the pre-Islamic period’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whoever has racist feelings in his heart of the size of mustard seed, on the Day of Judgment Allah will raise him with the Arabs of the time of Jahiliyah (dark age).’”
